name: systemd
description: System and service manager for Linux.
summary: Contributors may use generative AI to help write code and documentation, but must review and edit the output, understand and be able to explain it, and ensure license compatibility. AI tools must not be listed as authors, and must not open pull requests or issues, write issues, review comments, or mailing-list posts for contributors; commit messages and pull request descriptions may be AI-assisted if reviewed.

evidence.quote: You may use generative AI and LLM tools ("AI") to help create contributions, as long as you review and edit what they produce so it follows the project guidelines.
You must be able to explain every part of your contribution and why it was done that way, and you own the code like any other code you wrote.
Do not submit AI-generated code that you do not understand.
If you cannot explain the code you contributed, your contribution will not be merged and any further pull requests will likely not get reviewed.

Make sure your contribution, including any AI-generated code, is compatible with the project's license as documented in [`LICENSES/README.md`](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/main/LICENSES/README.md).
Do not list AI tools as author or co-author, or credit them in any way that suggests ownership.
Do not let an AI agent open pull requests or post for you.

Specifically, we do not allow the use of such tools to communicate on your behalf. You must speak for yourself. It is not permissible to let such tools open pull requests or issues, leave or respond to comments, or post to the systemd-devel mailing list.
